- Model tends to overestimate prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes.
- Forecast often peaks too early or too high, then underestimates the subsequent correction or continuation.
- Mean reversion is under-predicted — model fails to recognize that prices often return to prior levels after sharp moves.
- Overshoot after spikes: model reacts too aggressively to short-term volatility, leading to overcorrection in the next period.
- Lagged bias: model consistently underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast horizon, especially when true values are rising.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts show persistent underestimation of late-period price increases, particularly in the last 10–15 days.
- Model exhibits “sticky” behavior — fails to adjust downward when true values show downward momentum, even after prior overestimation.
